proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true admissions lag is closer to 2 weeks (or varies over time), forecasts may show phase error (peak timing off by ~1 week) and reduced stability across rolling splits due to misalignment.
proposals.rationale: Baseline stable choice aligned with prior best spec and analyst constraint to stay within SEIRS + delayed_I. A 1-week lag is mechanistically plausible for admissions vs. underlying infectious proxy and tends to be less delay-sensitive than longer lags in short (n_train=31) series.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Risk of over-lagging for this age group/series, producing smeared or late peaks and higher split-to-split variability if the effective lag is shorter or changes across the season.
proposals.rationale: Alternative lag within the allowed {1,2} to address observed delay sensitivity without adding complexity. Useful when hospitalization timing is systematically more delayed relative to I-proxy, potentially improving peak alignment while remaining parsimonious.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Fractional dynamics may be fragile/weakly identified in short training windows, leading to parameter drift across rolling splits and occasional over-smoothing or exaggerated persistence in forecasts.
proposals.rationale: Single complexity toggle (fractional dynamics) paired with the more stable 1-week delay to capture moderate peakiness and high rate scale while prioritizing rolling stability. Fractional SEIRS can flexibly represent memory/heterogeneity effects without changing observation semantics.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Compounded sensitivity: if either fractional memory or the 2-week lag is mis-specified, errors can amplify (late peaks + overly persistent tails), increasing rolling instability relative to the fractional+delay=1 option.
proposals.rationale: Fractional candidate with 2-week delay to cover the plausible longer admissions lag while still respecting the constraint of only varying (fractional, delay). This can help if both memory effects and a longer reporting/admission lag are present.
